speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your infant is suffering from bilious vomiting and an inability to pass meconium. To ensure we don't miss a surgical emergency, can you tell me exactly how many hours of age the baby was when they failed to pass their first stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Meconium Ileus.
The inability to pass meconium at birth combined with bilious vomiting and abdominal distension in a newborn is highly suggestive of meconium ileus until proven otherwise, often indicating an underlying Cystic Fibrosis diagnosis. I am requesting an abdominal X-ray and a sweat chloride test to confirm.
